commit.message:
AES-GCM-SIV: no-op on zero-length update and clear stale AAD on reuse

The default-provider AES-GCM-SIV implementation treated a zero-length
AAD update as a reset: aes_gcm_siv_aad() freed the AAD accumulated
so far, cleared its length, and returned success.  This meant
that an application passing AAD in multiple chunks, of which some
might have zero length, would have the previous AAD chunks effectively
unauthenticated.  Remove the AAD reset logic for zero-length updates.

Also, on context reinitialization, the AAD was not reset, which meant
that any AAD accumulated from the previous context usage were also
included in the AAD of the new message.  This applied
to a reinitialization with a new key or nonce, as well as
to a reinitialization without either after a completed operation, which
restarts the operation under the same key and nonce.  Reset the AAD
reset in both cases.  A parameters-only reinitialization before
the payload still keeps the AAD accumulated so far.

Fixes: CVE-2026-88823
